paras: The killing of Lee Aderholt was the fatal shooting of a 17-year-old at a magic lantern show at Caleb Carpenter's store near Cherryville, Gaston County, North Carolina, on the night of Saturday, June 30, 1888, by one of the twin brothers Bill and Dan Thornburg. A Raleigh dispatch reprinted in Ohio added that one of the brothers had been caught and lynched, but later North Carolina reports showed both brothers alive, one at large and the other jailed and then bailed.

The Charlotte Chronicle described the Thornburgs as "two notorious characters, who usually have several cases in every court," and as twins "very similar in appearance." Aderholt was the son of Emanuel Aderholt, a former treasurer of Gaston County.

According to the Chronicle, the brothers tried to force their way into the show without paying and were ejected, after which four shots were fired. One bullet struck Aderholt, who was waiting for the performance to begin, just below the right eye, and he died within fifteen minutes. Two shots hit the showman in the hip and arm; the Chronicle called his wounds serious "but not fatally," while a Raleigh special in the Atlanta Constitution said he was injured "fatally."

Witnesses could not say which twin drew a revolver, and a Raleigh correspondent expected the resemblance between them to make it hard to prove which one fired. Both brothers escaped and were described in early July as fugitives from justice.

A Raleigh special dated July 9, printed in the Stark County Democrat of Canton, Ohio, closed with a courier report that one of the brothers "was caught and lynched last night." No other report of a lynching appears in the coverage, and in August the Charlotte Democrat reported that Bill Thornburg was back in his old neighborhood "defiant of the law," with officers said to be afraid to arrest him.

In September the Governor offered a reward of $200 for each brother, who were believed to have fled to South Carolina. The Gastonia Gazette reported in late October that Deputy Carpenter had captured Dan Thornburg in a strawstack and that he was in jail. A November item reported that Dan had been admitted to bail, and no report of a trial was found.

The case ran mainly in North Carolina and South Carolina papers, where the Charlotte Chronicle's account appeared under headings such as "Murder in Gaston County." Raleigh specials carried the story to Richmond, Atlanta and Ohio, and the Ohio version, headed "Death at a Magic Lantern Show," called the brothers "two toughs" and was the only one to add the lynching.

When the Governor's reward was announced, the Gold Leaf of Henderson used the case to argue that "Justice is too tardy in North Carolina," saying that slow authorities led communities to act "in lynching parties frequently." The Fisherman & Farmer reprinted that editorial with the words "We agree with the Gold Leaf."

The claim that a Thornburg was lynched rests on a single courier item in one Ohio reprint, while later local reports, including the Gastonia Gazette's, show both brothers living through November 1888. Reports also differed on which twin fired, with the Charlotte Democrat naming Bill and others saying the witnesses were unsure, and on whether the killing took place in Gaston or Lincoln County.

reader.title: Killing of Lee Aderholt
bases: The documented violence is a shooting by two brothers into a show audience that killed Lee Aderholt (A1, A2, A3); the single report that one brother was lynched (A6) is contradicted by later reports of both brothers alive, sought and one jailed (A7, A8, A11).

The only lynching claim is a courier item that one Thornburg brother 'was caught and lynched' (A6); Bill Thornburg was reported back in his neighborhood in August (A7), the Governor offered rewards for both brothers in September (A8, A9), and Dan was jailed in October and admitted to bail in November (A11, A12), so no one was killed by a mob; the killing of Aderholt was by two brothers, not a group of three or more acting as justice (A1, A3).
The shooting is corroborated by several independent reports (A1, A2, A4), but the lynching reported in A6 is contradicted by every later report showing both brothers alive (A7, A8, A11).

accounts.label: Charlotte Chronicle report
accounts.gist: The twins forced their way into a show without paying, were ejected, and four shots killed Aderholt and wounded the showman seriously but not fatally; the Thornburgs escaped.

accounts.label: Raleigh specials (early July)
accounts.gist: Same story from Raleigh; the Thornburgs fled and are fugitives, with the twins' resemblance expected to make it hard to prove which fired.

accounts.label: Raleigh special of July 9 with courier 'LATER'
accounts.gist: Repeats the shooting and adds, by courier, that one brother was caught and lynched the previous night.

accounts.label: Later North Carolina reports
accounts.gist: Bill was back in his neighborhood in August, the Governor offered rewards for both in September, and Dan was captured, jailed and admitted to bail in October and November.

framing.detail: North Carolina and South Carolina papers ran it as 'Murder in Gaston County', calling the twins 'two notorious characters, who usually have several cases in every court'.
Out-of-state papers carried Raleigh specials; the Ohio version headed 'Death at a Magic Lantern Show' called the brothers 'two toughs' and added the unconfirmed lynching.
The Gold Leaf cited the case to complain that 'Justice is too tardy' and that slow authorities drive communities to 'lynching parties', without endorsing a lynching here.

versions.value: one Thornburg brother caught and lynched
both brothers escaped and remained alive: Bill at large in August, rewards for both in September, Dan jailed in October and bailed in November

conflicts.note: The later, local North Carolina reports, including the Gastonia Gazette via A11, are the better evidence; the courier item in A6 appears only in one Ohio reprint.
No report of the showman's death appears in the coverage.
Several reports stress that the twins' resemblance left witnesses unsure.
Most reports, including the Gastonia Gazette item, place it in Gaston county.
